final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative neutralization of a transmembrane acidic residue is likely to disrupt transport energetics while retaining side-chain size and hydrogen-bonding capacity, reducing folding risk.

Removal of this buried transmembrane positive charge could abolish charge coupling or conformational transitions. Alanine remains helix-compatible, although loss of stabilizing interactions creates some abundance risk.

Eliminating a bulky aromatic residue in a transmembrane substrate-recognition region is likely to strongly impair transport. Confidence is lower because the packing perturbation may also reduce protein abundance.
